phrases.text: So welcome back again.
It's time to solve
one more problem.
Now, in this problem,
we have a tower
and two points are on the same side of that tower. These two points are forty meter apart.
From the nearer point,
the angle of elevation is sixty degree,
and from the farther point, the angle of elevation is thirty degrees.
And we need to find the height of the tower.
Let the distance of the nearer point from the tower be x meter.
So the farther point will be x plus forty meters from the tower.
Here,
tangent is the most useful ratio.
Why tangent?
Because tangent connects height and base.
Tan theta is equal to height by base.
So from the nearer point,
tan sixty degrees is equal to h by x,
which gives
root three is equal to h by x.
That means
h is equal to x root three.
Okay,
keep this aside for a second.
We will use the same height from the other point also.
Now, from the farther point,
tan thirty degrees is equal to h by x plus forty.
So one by root three is equal to h by x plus forty.
But we already found that h is equal to x root three,
so put x root three in place of h.
Then it becomes
one by root three is equal to
x root three by x plus forty.
After cross-multiplication,
x plus forty is equal to three x.
So forty is equal to two x and x is equal to twenty. Done. We got the distance of the nearer point.
But wait,
the question is not asking for this distance.
The question is asking for the tower height.
So use h is equal to x root three.
H is equal to twenty root three
meter.
Hence,
the height of the tower is twenty root three meters.
